$comment: Which cells the evaluation harness measures, and which cell supplies each one's
'asked in the wrong cell' items. This lived as a dict in scripts/evaluation/cli.py while
there were two cells; phase2.0a takes it to four, which is where a hardcoded map stops
being cheaper than the file. JSON has no comments, so the reasoning travels in `note` —
the neighbour choice is a decision and it should be readable where it is made, not only
`gated` is whether the four per-cell trust gates are claimed for this cell, and it is not
the same question as whether the harness can measure it. The FDA cells are measurable and
NOT gated: Phase 1 Go is still required before any Phase 2 cell is declared gated

mfds_samd.note: Unchanged. The cross-domain neighbour it has always had — this cell is gated and its golden set is a phase 1.6 gate input, so its composition does not move as a side effect of adding FDA.

mfds_cosmetic.note: Unchanged, for the same reason as mfds_samd.

fda_samd.note: Both, deliberately. fda_cosmetic is the cross-DOMAIN neighbour: same authority, same language, and the two FDA cells already share Parts 7 and 11, so declining requires respecting the cell scope rather than noticing a change of subject. mfds_samd is the cross-AUTHORITY neighbour: same subject, so retrieval will find topically similar in-scope clauses and answer a Korean question out of US law — a confident wrong answer with the wrong jurisdiction's numbers, which is the one that would actually hurt a customer. They are different failure modes and picking one leaves the other unmeasured.

fda_cosmetic.note: Both, for the same reasons as fda_samd.
